SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — NOT AN ACTUAL GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT

Northstar Department of Resident Services

Digital Access Strategy 2027–2030

Publication date: 2026-02-12

1. Executive Summary

The Northstar Department of Resident Services (NDRS) will modernize how residents apply for and manage public benefits. Residents currently navigate separate portals for assistance programs, repeat identity checks, and receive status notices through inconsistent channels. The department's strategic need is a single, accessible citizen-service experience that works on mobile devices, supports multiple languages, and lets a resident see application status without calling a service center.

2. Current-State Challenges

Legacy case systems exchange data through nightly files. Staff re-enter information when a resident reports a change to more than one program. Contact-center teams lack a consolidated view of prior notices and open requests. These conditions lengthen handling time and make it difficult to measure whether residents complete a service journey.

3. Modernization Priorities

Priority A — Unified access: provide one sign-on, guided intake, document upload, and status tracking across participating programs.

3. Modernization Priorities

Priority B — Reusable integration: expose governed APIs and event notifications without replacing every system of record at once.

3. Modernization Priorities

Priority C — Inclusive delivery: conform to WCAG 2.2 AA, provide translated content, test with residents, and maintain assisted-service options.

4. Measures of Progress

Measure | Synthetic baseline | 2030 target
Digital application completion | 58 percent | 82 percent
Status-related calls | 420,000 per year | 30 percent reduction
Average change-report handling | 18 minutes | 10 minutes

5. Governance

The Office of Digital Services will sponsor the portfolio. Program operations, security, privacy, procurement, and the resident advisory panel will review releases quarterly. This strategy describes direction and does not itself authorize purchasing.

Northstar Department of Resident Services
Benefits Stewardship and Payment Quality Plan
Publication date: 2028-05-10
Last updated: 2028-06-01

1. Payment Quality

NDRS will improve benefit correctness by identifying both overpayments and underpayments before issuance when practical. The department uses the phrase payment accuracy to include the correct recipient, amount, and period of eligibility. Quality-control samples will distinguish agency processing error, incomplete information, and timing differences rather than labeling every discrepancy as intentional misconduct.

2. Program Integrity

The stewardship program will combine preventive controls, post-payment review, and targeted case examination. Cross-program data matching may flag inconsistent identity, income, residency, or household information for review. A match is an investigative lead, not a final determination, and trained staff must document resolution.

3. Fraud Risk Management

Potential fraud means deliberate deception for an unauthorized benefit. Detection analytics will prioritize unusual patterns, coordinated account activity, and repeated document attributes. The agency will monitor false positives, provide notice and appeal rights, and prohibit automatic adverse action based solely on a model score.

4. Loss Prevention and Recovery

Improper payment reduction includes process correction, recipient education, verification at application or renewal, and recovery when legally authorized. The plan also calls this work benefits assurance and leakage control. These related terms may appear in different program materials even when the underlying modernization need is shared.

5. Technology Needs

NDRS needs configurable rules, entity resolution, case-review workflow, evidence tracking, audit history, and outcome measurement. Any future acquisition must separate detection from adjudication and provide transparent reasons that reviewers can evaluate.
